result.title: MoSoLoco: Monocular 3D Human Localization through Visual Latent Features and Social Context
result.summary: Estimating the metric 3D position of people from a monocular camera is important for robot navigation and motion prediction. Lightweight pose-based localizers are attractive for robotic hardware with limited computational resources because they operate on compact 2D keypoints. However, they typically discard the richer visual representations computed by the pose estimator. We introduce MoSoLoco, a per-frame monocular 3D human localizer that combines the pose detector's internal visual features with the detected 2D skeleton, without requiring an additional RGB or depth encoder. MoSoLoco can further incorporate sparse same-frame multi-person context to refine individual position estimates. Experiments on JRDB and NuScenes show that reusing pose-detector representations improves localization, reducing the best JRDB error by approximately 23 percent relative to the strongest evaluated keypoint-based baseline. A sparse social-interaction module incorporates nearby detections from the same image for further refinement. Controlled trajectory-forecasting experiments show downstream benefits, while the complete pipeline remains suitable for efficient Jetson AGX Xavier inference.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MoSoLoco，一种逐帧单目人体 3D 定位方法：不加额外 RGB 或深度编码器，而是直接复用姿态检测器的内部视觉特征与 2D 骨架，并可融合同帧稀疏多人上下文细化位置；在 JRDB 与 NuScenes 上验证精度提升，且可在 Jetson AGX Xavier 上高效推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察——紧凑的 2D 关键点表征会丢弃检测器内部更丰富的视觉特征，而复用这些特征可改善下游估计——可能为 LVR 中「视觉细节是否在内部状态中保留、紧凑中间表征是否造成信息坍缩」提供跨领域类比，但任务为度量定位而非推理状态生成，需较多核查。
